news_findings.title: Lyft CEO takes blame for 'extra zero' in Q4 earnings release
news_findings.content:
During its quarterly call with investors, Lyft CFO Erin Brewer said the figure was incorrect and that the actual increase will be 50 basis points, or 0.5%. That means Lyft's adjusted profit margin as a percentage of bookings will be 2.1% this year, up from 1.6% in 2023. The mistake also appeared in Lyft's slide deck.

"Look, it was a bad error, and that's on me," Risher said Wednesday.

The stock was still up after the correction, because the numbers beat analysts' estimates, but it lost much of its initial pop, equal to over $2 billion in market cap.

"We had thousands of eyes, we've got a process on this that is nuts," Risher said. "It's a terrible thing. It is an extra zero that slipped into a press release." [...] Risher said the company discovered the error after it became clear on the earnings call that there was a lot of interest in the margin. When a team member identified the problem, Risher said he could see her "jaw drop."

"Thank goodness we caught it pretty fast, and we issued an immediate correction," he said.

Lyft shares jumped 35% on Wednesday to $16.09, their best day since the company's IPO in 2019. However, the stock is still about 77% below its debut price.

Lyft reported $1.22 billion in revenue for the quarter, an increase of 4% from $1.175 billion a year earlier. The company posted adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, which was above the 8 cents expected by analysts, according to LSEG, formerly known as Refinitiv. [...] In this article

Lyft CEO David Risher took responsibility for the major error that appeared in the company's fourth-quarter earnings release, telling CNBC's "Squawk Box" that it's "super frustrating" for everyone on the team.

Shares of the ride-hailing company soared more than 60% after the report came out late Tuesday because the press release said Lyft would see margin expansion of 500 basis points, or 5%, in 2024, a huge increase for a business that has long struggled to turn a profit.

The company's strategic investment of over €16 billion in Germany is expected to bolster its operational capabilities, further enhancing its growth potential. SEATTLE—(BUSINESS WIRE) October 29, 2026—Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

•Net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion in the third quarter, compared with $180.2 billion in third quarter 2025. Excluding the $0.9 billion unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates throughout the quarter, net sales increased 13% compared with third quarter 2025. As a reminder, Prime Day timing shifted this year, with the event occurring in Q2 for most large countries. In 2025, Prime Day occurred entirely in Q3. Excluding this shift, third quarter year-over-year growth would have been approximately 400 basis points higher.

•North America segment sales increased 6% year-over-year to $112.9 billion. [...] Period ended 2026-09-30. news_findings.title: Meta (META) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates
news_findings.content:
This is CNBC's live coverage of Meta's 2026 third-quarter earnings.

Meta reported better-than-expected revenue in its third-quarter earnings report on Wednesday and issued strong guidance for the current period. The stock rose about 2.5% in extended trading.

It's not clear if earnings were comparable to the $5.75 per share expected by analysts.

Revenue jumped 26% from a year ago.

"We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model," said CEO Mark Zuckerberg in the earnings release.

For the fourth quarter, Meta said it expects revenue of between $73 billion and $76 billion, or $74.5 billion at the middle of the range. Analysts expected $73.73 billion, according to LSEG. [...] —Jonathan Vanian

Meta's Reality Labs division, which is tasked with developing virtual reality headsets and AI-powered wearable devices, is expected to post a loss of $4.54 billion while generating $513 million in sales for the third quarter, according to StreetAccount.

In July when Meta reported second-quarter earnings, the company revealed that the Reality Labs unit lost $4.62 billion while bringing in $431 million during the period.

With the VR market struggling to catch on with consumers, Zuckerberg has since shifted Reality Labs resources to center on more on AI-driven hardware products like the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses the company creates with eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica. [...] — Jonathan Vanian

Meta is offering $20 and $100 monthly subscription plans for Muse AI agent power users. Right now, Muse is free to use but requires a subscription to run it with Meta's latest model — Muse Wonder. The company is also charging developers $50 or $200 a month to access its most powerful Muse Wonder Full AI model via the Muse coding agent that debuted in early August.

Meta's nascent subscription efforts represent opportunities for the company to expand beyond online advertising, which is still its core money maker. Investors have been concerned about the Facebook parent's hefty AI investments relative to rivals like Alphabet and Amazon that have cloud computing businesses.

Business News›News›International›US News›SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. # SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. SoFi stock surges 7% on Trump tax plan hype — earnings buzz builds ahead of July 29. SoFi Technologies stock saw a 7% climb due to Trump's tax plan. The plan limits federal student loans, potentially benefiting private lenders like SoFi. Investors are optimistic, with the stock up over 100% in three months. SoFi's Q2 results are due on July 29. SoFi Technologies stock climbed 7% on Tuesday as investors responded to the latest policy changes proposed by US president Donald Trump, as per a report. His recently signed tax plan into law includes new limits on federal student loans, a move that could shift more borrowers toward private lenders like SoFi, and markets are taking notice, according to a TipRanks report. That gap in funding could create an opening for private loan providers, and SoFi, long known for its student loan and refinancing business, is well-positioned to benefit, as per the report. The market sees an opportunity for growth for the company, as a drop in federal support could drive more borrowers to its platform, and that’s what investors are betting on, according to the TipRanks report. SoFi stock has now increased more than 100% in the past three months, as reported by TipRanks. ## Earnings Buzz Builds Ahead of July 29 Report. The firm's stock rise comes as SoFi is going to post its second-quarter results on July 29, and investor expectations are already high, as reported by TipRanks. As per the TipRanks report, Wall Street analysts projected that the company will report earnings of $0.06 per share, increasing 500% from the year-ago quarter. With student lending now in focus because of Trump's tax bill, SoFi’s performance in that segment is expected to draw even closer attention this quarter, and a solid report might give the firm's stock another lift as "policy tailwinds and strong business fundamentals begin to align," wrote TipRanks in its report.

Title: SoFi Stock Forecast 2026: Latest News, Earnings, Risks and SOFI Price Prediction - zinpedia
## SoFi Stock Forecast 2026: Latest News, Earnings, Risks and SOFI Price Prediction. SoFi Technologies has grown from a student-loan refinancing company into a broad digital financial-services business. Today, its platform includes lending, banking, investing, credit cards and financial technology infrastructure. That wider business model has made **SoFi stock**, traded on Nasdaq under the ticker **SOFI**, popular among growth investors. Supporters see a fast-growing digital bank with rising membership, expanding revenue and improving profitability. Critics argue that the stock already reflects a large amount of future growth and remains exposed to credit conditions, interest rates, regulation and competition. As of July 24, 2026, SOFI shares were trading near $16.59, giving the company a market value of approximately $22.9 billion. Its trailing price-to-earnings ratio was around 36.9, based on the latest available market data. The question for investors is therefore not simply whether SoFi is growing. The more important question is whether the company can grow fast enough—and profitably enough—to justify its valuation. This article examines the latest SoFi stock news, financial results, growth drivers, risks, and a scenario-based price prediction for 2026. It is not personalized financial advice, and no stock-price forecast is guaranteed. ## What Is SoFi Technologies and How Does It Make Money? SoFi Technologies is a digital financial-services company and bank holding company. Through SoFi Bank and its broader technology platform, it offers products that help customers borrow, save, spend, and invest money. Lending has historically generated a large share of SoFi’s revenue. This part of the company is important because it allows SoFi to build longer relationships with members. The company reported that Financial Services products reached approximately 19.3 million in the first quarter of 2026. The Technology Platform gives SoFi an opportunity to earn business-to-business revenue rather than depending entirely on consumer loans and banking products. First-quarter 2026 Technology Platform revenue fell 27% year over year to approximately $75.1 million, partly because a large client completed its transition away from the platform before the end of 2025. SoFi reported strong operating results for the first quarter of 2026. The company also stated that its Loan Platform Business is able to make fee income from originating loans for partners and keeping the servicing rights.

Separately, NIO China agreed to acquire 10.0% of Geely’s Haohan Energy for cash that will fund Haohan Energy’s purchase of certain NIO charging assets. Plans to extend battery swapping to Geely-related vehicles remain preliminary.

## NIO Inc. Reports Unaudited Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NIO (NYSE: NIO) reported second quarter 2026 total revenues of RMB32,136.9 million (US$4,736.4 million), up 69.1% year over year and 25.9% quarter over quarter. Vehicle sales reached RMB29,058.2 million, up 80.1% year over year, with vehicle margin at 18.5%. [...] NIO delivered 107,658 vehicles in Q2 2026, up 49.4% year over year and 29.0% quarter over quarter, including NIO, ONVO and FIREFLY brands. Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments and long-term time deposits totaled RMB56.7 billion as of June 30, 2026. news_findings.title: Lyft CEO takes blame for 'extra zero' in Q4 earnings release
news_findings.content:
During its quarterly call with investors, Lyft CFO Erin Brewer said the figure was incorrect and that the actual increase will be 50 basis points, or 0.5%. That means Lyft's adjusted profit margin as a percentage of bookings will be 2.1% this year, up from 1.6% in 2023. The mistake also appeared in Lyft's slide deck.

"Look, it was a bad error, and that's on me," Risher said Wednesday.

The stock was still up after the correction, because the numbers beat analysts' estimates, but it lost much of its initial pop, equal to over $2 billion in market cap.

"We had thousands of eyes, we've got a process on this that is nuts," Risher said. "It's a terrible thing. It is an extra zero that slipped into a press release." [...] Risher said the company discovered the error after it became clear on the earnings call that there was a lot of interest in the margin. When a team member identified the problem, Risher said he could see her "jaw drop."

"Thank goodness we caught it pretty fast, and we issued an immediate correction," he said.

Lyft shares jumped 35% on Wednesday to $16.09, their best day since the company's IPO in 2019. However, the stock is still about 77% below its debut price.

Lyft reported $1.22 billion in revenue for the quarter, an increase of 4% from $1.175 billion a year earlier. The company posted adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, which was above the 8 cents expected by analysts, according to LSEG, formerly known as Refinitiv. [...] In this article

Lyft CEO David Risher took responsibility for the major error that appeared in the company's fourth-quarter earnings release, telling CNBC's "Squawk Box" that it's "super frustrating" for everyone on the team.

Shares of the ride-hailing company soared more than 60% after the report came out late Tuesday because the press release said Lyft would see margin expansion of 500 basis points, or 5%, in 2024, a huge increase for a business that has long struggled to turn a profit.
